sections.markdown:
## C2 — Continuation facts, then confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: perception versus reaction time, flood depths, slowing before versus braking in a curve, horn use and signals versus brake lights
Continuation facts for visual search, flooding, space and communication, plus confusable pairs among stopping-distance parts, flood depths, curve speed, horn use and signals; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Driving skills come only through practice and experience, and the manual offers these tips as things to practice to become a safer, more skillful driver. [A01]
Why it matters: group visual search; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A02
How far ahead you can look depends on where you drive, and in cities and urban areas you may not see as far as on a highway. [A02]
Why it matters: group visual search; confusable city versus highway sight distance.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A02
Search to the sides of your vehicle to see whether other road users are about to cross your path. [A02]
Why it matters: group visual search; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A02
Speed should come down before the curve, because hard braking after you have entered it could make the tires lose traction. [A02]
Why it matters: group speed; confusable slowing before versus braking in the curve.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A04
Flooding can come from rivers and streams overflowing, dams or levees breaking, run-off from deep snow or any heavy rainfall, and floodwater gathers on roads, bridges and low areas. [A04]
Why it matters: group flooding; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A04
Take special care at night around possible flooding, when visibility is limited. [A04]
Why it matters: group flooding; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A04
Six inches of water is enough to reach the underside of most passenger cars, while two feet of moving water can carry away even SUVs and pickups. [A04]
Why it matters: group flooding; confusable six inches versus two feet.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A04
If no other route exists, drive to higher ground and wait for the floodwater to go down. [A04]
Why it matters: group flooding; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A05
Perception time is about recognizing that you must stop, while reaction time is about moving your foot from the gas to the brake, and both average ¾ second to 1 second. [A05]
Why it matters: group stopping distance; confusable perception versus reaction.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A06
You can test how well you judge the four-second gap by guessing how many seconds away an object is and then counting the seconds it takes to reach it. [A06]
Why it matters: group following distance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A07
Make room for vehicles joining a multi-lane or limited access road by moving over a lane or adjusting your speed. [A07]
Why it matters: group side space; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A08
You can help the driver behind you keep a safe distance by holding a steady speed, signaling early and leaving extra room ahead before you slow down or turn. [A08]
Why it matters: group rear space; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A08
Under normal circumstances a light tap on the horn should be all you need. [A08]
Why it matters: group horn; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A08
On rainy, snowy or foggy days the manual says to drive with your low-beam lights on and to slow down. [A08]
Why it matters: group headlights; confusable low beam versus high beam.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A09
Once a lane change, turn or merge is finished, cancel your signal so other drivers are not confused. [A09]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A09
The horn is a tool for getting attention when needed, but near blind pedestrians it should not be used at all. [A09]
Why it matters: group horn; confusable warning tap versus no horn.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A10
Brake lights show you are slowing, but you should also signal before slowing when you leave a road that has no separate turn or exit lane. [A10]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable brake lights versus turn signal.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0102]
